method: 10,000 deals driven end to end through the real settlement engine via fastapi TestClient against pact.main:app in a single shared session (context manager shares one event loop portal). Demo mode forced by popping PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID/PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET/LLM_API_KEY/PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID/CHANNEL3_API_KEY before import; PACT_DB_PATH set to a temp dir (dev DB at data/pact.db untouched). Lifecycle per deal: POST /api/deals, negotiate/run, pay (demo captures instantly to paid_held; no pay/confirm needed), deliver, verify, with resume loops through injected 502s (deal stays 'verifying') and revision rounds (re-deliver then verify again) until a terminal state. Failure injection: get_agent_payment_service monkeypatched per deal with a fail-once stub in the shape of tests/hardening_test.py PART I (FailLegStub): 0-2 randomly chosen legs raise PaymentError on the first send under the deterministic idempotency key, before the simulator records anything; the resume re-sends under the same key and succeeds. Money audit in integer cents from the amounts on the stub's successful payout/refund calls, cross-checked against each leg's recorded status (done => exactly one money call). persistence.save_all was patched to a no-op for speed; the in-memory store is what the API reads/writes, so settlement logic is unaffected. Negotiation concession behavior was randomized via buyer_max/seller_floor draws inside each scenario's price band (plus a 2% adversarial floor>ceiling walkaway); bond percents 10-30; delivery qualities auto/weak/cheat/poor at 50/15/15/20. Deal records were deleted from the in-memory store after auditing to bound memory; only violating deals would have been kept (none).
